facts.text: Stronach was first called Paggeotville before brothers John and Adam Stronach built a sawmill in 1841, renaming the village.
The Stronach Rail Bridge, erected in 1887, still stands on original wooden abutments, a relic of the town’s railroad era.
A post office opened in Stronach on August 9, 1866, and operated until December 21, 1893, with some records extending to 1954 or 1983.
The Little Manistee River runs along Stronach’s southern edge, flowing into Manistee Lake, which borders the community’s western side.
By 1855, Stronach Township was officially organized as one of Manistee County’s original three townships, the first non‑native settlement in the county.
In May 1885, a wildfire swept through Old Stronach, destroying most of the village and marking the end of its early mill era.
